correctness.rationale: All essential inferences and computations verify exactly. Count lemma (orthogonality iff ratio-counts (2,2,2)) is correct: n0+n1*w+n2*w2=(n0-n2)+(n1-n2)*w with {1,w} Z-free, so zero iff n0=n1=n2=2; row-sum-zero characterization follows. Hand R3* checks correct: <R1,R3*> ratios (0,2,0,1,2,1) counts (2,2,2); <R2,R3*> ratios (0,2,1,2,1,0) counts (2,2,2). Canonical 2-border lemma proof is sound: tail of row2 has (1,2,2) counts so column perm fixing col1 sorts to R2 preserving dephasing/BH; columns are orthogonal via unitarity (HH*=6I => H*H=6I) so col2 tail is {w,w,w2,w2} and row perm fixing rows1-2 sorts to C2 preserving dephasing/BH. Search completeness verified independently: pools C4/C5/C6 each 12 =4!/(1!1!2!) correct; 12+12+24=48 checks with pruning on necessary row-orthogonality is exhaustive because any BH completion must satisfy row-orthogonality; column orthogonality then automatic for square unimodular matrices and is confirmed a posteriori by verifier. Independent re-enumeration (complex arithmetic, 30 vectors with col1=0 and (2,2,2), 12/12/6 split by col2) reproduces depth-4 12->1 (R4=(0,1,2,0,2,1)), depth-5 12->2 (A=(0,2,1,2,0,1), B=(0,2,2,1,1,0), A perp B), depth-6 24->2 ordered (1 unordered up to R5<->R6 which fixes C2). Eisenstein Gram verifier correct: (a1+b1w)(a2+b2w)=(a1a2-b1b2)+(a1b2+a2b1-b1b2)w using w2=-1-w, conj (a-b,-b), G=H conj(H^T)=6I for rows and columns, alphabet/dephasing/border/counts all PASS; cross-checked via complex Gram (max off-diag err 2.2e-16). Symmetry and diagonal-1 verified (matrix symmetric, diag all 0). Defect integer system correct: Re*2 gives r=2/-1, Im*2/sqrt3 gives s=0/+1/-1 for mu3 and remap/smap for F6 verified against cos/sin; Fraction rank 25/null11/defect0 (dephased null0) vs Fourier 21/15/4 (dephased 4) reproduced exactly and via modular rank over 3 primes (1000003,1000033,998244353) plus trivial-phase directions in kernel. Haagerup enumeration correct: exponent formula (eij+ekl-eil-ekj) mod3/6, 1296 quadruples, solution {1,w,w2} 576/360/360 vs F6 all six 6th roots, invariance under monomial equivalence holds (phases cancel; spot-checked 3 random monomial transforms preserve set). Draft honestly separates proved (a-e, Gram, Fourier-inequivalence) vs computed certificates vs conjecture (explicit monomial map to frozen published S6 Tao array not machine-checked, stated as catalog-supported only; uniqueness slice-local; defect convention stated). No floating point used; scripts re-ran exit 0 in <1s. No correctness defect requiring repair.

originality.rationale: No substantively new mathematical object or gap is established. The exhibited H is admitted by the draft (Sec.8: 'the matrix coincides (up to the bordered gauge) with the known Tao-type example') to be monomial-equivalent to the known isolated Tao/S6 BH(6,3) example listed in Tadej-Zyczkowski quant-ph/0607136 as the single BH(6,3) class. It shares the characteristic Tao profile: alphabet mu3, defect 0, Lambda subset mu3 size 3, symmetric diagonal-1 form. No new inequivalent Hadamard is claimed or proved; no explicit monomial map to a frozen published S6 array was built, so even catalog-equivalence is not machine-checked, only invariant-match + citation. Fourier-inequivalence (defect 0 vs 4, Lambda 3 vs 6) is not original: any mu3 matrix has Lambda subset mu3, while F6 contains zeta=exp(pi i/3) not in mu3, so inequivalence follows trivially from alphabet without frequency counts; defect 0 for Tao vs 4 for F6 is textbook literature recomputed with the same code. The only novelty asserted is 'first certified completion-or-gap verdict for this doubly-sorted R3* slice' — i.e., that one coordinate prefix extends with slice-local uniqueness. This is timestamp/failed-search reasoning, not substantive difference: it is a coordinate-dependent corollary of the known singleton classification (take Tao representative, sort to R2/C2, read off third-row orbit). Independent check shows R3* is one of 4 prefixes with [0,1] orthogonal to R1,R2 ([0,1,0,2,1,2],[0,1,0,2,2,1],[0,1,2,0,1,2],[0,1,2,0,2,1]) in the same R2-stabilizer orbit (swap cols 3<->4, 5<->6), and all 4 give identical outcome (1 R4, 2 ordered sols). Choosing R3* among them is arbitrary gauge choice, not a new equivalence class. A gap (which would be structural restriction beyond n-mod-3) was not found; existence of a Tao-equivalent completion was. Compared substantively to nearest priors — Tadej-Zyczkowski catalog (Tao/S6 + Fourier F6 + defect/equivalence), Bengtsson et al. MUB-6 bases, Szollosi/Karlsson continuous families (positive defect, transverse to Butson locus) — the candidate adds no inequivalent family, no new invariant, and no decided gap. Hence originality FAIL.

value.rationale: Result is not independently worth finding later. The slice R3*=[1,w,1,w2,w,w2] is an arbitrary third-row pattern among 4 equivalent prefixes (9 total orthogonal to R1,R2 without col2 fixing), with no independent motivation for this pattern over its orbit-mates; all 4 extend identically, so no distinctive structural insight. Outcome (A) existence of a Tao-equivalent matrix provides no new quantum-design input (same monomial class gives same design up to relabeling/phases) and no structural gap (which would have restricted BH(6,3) beyond trivial divisibility); it is a re-expression of a known object in canonical border gauge. Enumeration is trivial (48 inner checks, 1e-4 s, pools 12) — not a reusable pruning benchmark; column pruning is noted redundant, defect/Haagerup are standard textbook verifications for Tao vs Fourier. Uniqueness up to swapping last two rows (both col2=w2) is a gauge artifact, not a classification advance; global BH(6,3) single-class status is cited, not re-proved, and slice-local uniqueness does not advance it. Fallback R4-catalog (1 vector) is the same trivial depth-4 statement. A future researcher seeking BH(6,3) would look up the global Tao singleton classification, not this coordinate slice; the slice verdict would not be searched for, cited, or built upon except as a tiny corollary. This is exactly the SCOPE value-reject category: correct and narrowly new coordinate fact but textbook restatement (known Tao matrix sorted), mere parameter choice (which orthogonal third row), and unexplained enumeration (why this R3* matters for MUB-6 is not shown — MUB relevance requires inequivalent bases, not same-class re-gauging). Hence value FAIL even though correct.
